bullets.title: August NFP +162K crushes 55K consensus; Fed hike odds surge to ~60% for Sep 16
bullets.body: The August payroll report delivered a 5-month high headline (+162K vs. 55K consensus, prior July revised from -23K to +21K), with a 3-month average of +71K. Unemployment held at 4.1%, participation rose 22bps, and employment diffusion hit a near 2-year high of 55.6%. Wage growth printed +0.3% MoM/+3.1% YoY. Multiple desks flagged the report as hawkish for bonds but debated equity implications—September FOMC is now live at 54–62% hike odds. September 11 CPI remains the decisive swing factor.

bullets.title: Fed's Waller sets high bar for September hike; only fires if CPI > 0.3% MoM
bullets.body: Governor Waller signaled he would hold in September if August core PCE tracks ≤0.25% MoM, tempering initial post-Warsh hawkishness. Waller sees inflation progressing, noted the disinflation trend in 3-month annualized PCE (falling to 3.05%), and characterized policy as 'only slightly restrictive.' September hike odds fell from ~70% pre-Waller to ~54% post-comments but rebounded to 60%+ after the NFP beat.

bullets.title: ECB near-certain to hike to 2.5% next week; third hike now majority probability
bullets.body: Euro area HICP rose to 3.3% in August on 14.3% YoY energy inflation; core held at 2.41%. JPMorgan and Goldman both expect the ECB to hike 25bp on September 10 and price in a third move by December 2026, driven by the US-Iran conflict's energy shock (TTF 50%+ above June ECB assumption) and resilient euro area GDP (tracking ~1.4% annualized). Neutral rate estimates are being revised higher to 2.25–2.50%.

bullets.title: 10-year yields breach 4.75–4.80%, 30-year at multi-decade highs; global tightening cycle broadening
bullets.body: The US 10-year hit 4.76–4.78%, its highest since January 2025, while the US 30-year eclipsed 5% with the longest streak above that level since 2006. German 30-year yields reached 15-year highs; French 30-year hit September 2008 highs. JPMorgan attributes the move to cycle fundamentals (AI capex debt issuance, 6%+ nominal GDP, 4.1% unemployment) rather than fiscal distress. The environment is 'Quad 2' per Hedgeye—rising yields, large-cap over small-cap, software over semis.

bullets.title: JPMorgan shifts equity stance to Tactically Cautious/Neutral; recommends reducing net longs
bullets.body: JPM Market Intelligence pivoted to Tactically Cautious amid: (1) Fed live for September, (2) momentum factor down 21–34% from June highs (well outside the 10–15% typical drawdown), (3) credit spreads expected to widen post-Labor Day, (4) September's historically worst seasonal month for SPX, and (5) choppy 3–4 week positioning window. They favor Mag7 over semis/AI hardware, and large-cap banks and consumer discretionary over momentum names. Post-midterm seasonality (+5–15% at 3–12 month tenors) is the bull case.

bullets.title: AI capex remains massive growth driver for US economy; circular financing and systemic concentration risks flagged
bullets.body: Hyperscalers are spending ~$700B this year on AI capex, roughly half of projected 2% US GDP growth. Anthropic signed a $35B compute deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda (at $16M/MW—60% above prior market); total AI-related corporate debt commitments may reach $3–7T through 2030. GS and 22V warn that if OpenAI or a key frontier lab fails, the contagion to NVDA, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, and ORCL could be severe. The S&P 500 cash return ratio hit a historic low of 56%, driven by AI buildout CapEx displacing buybacks.

bullets.title: Warsh at Jackson Hole: hawkish on r-star, financial conditions 'only slightly restrictive'
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh's August 28 speech argued secular stagnation has reversed, called for focus on money supply alongside rates, and concluded that broad financial conditions—including equity markets and credit spreads—suggest policy is barely restrictive. His reaction function has drifted hawkish; he dismissed the global savings glut rationale for low r*. The speech was widely interpreted as validating 1–2 more hikes and pushed the September meeting to 'live.'

bullets.title: GS Prime: hedge funds net bought equities for first time in 3 weeks; Comm Services, Financials, Info Tech led
bullets.body: GS Prime Services weekly showed fundamental L/S down 0.55% (short-side losses) while systematic L/S rose +1.67%. Overall gross leverage fell 1.9 pts to 304%. Single stocks were net bought for the first time in 3 weeks, with long buys outpacing short sales 2.5:1. Healthcare sentiment rolling over from all-time highs; HFs rotating from HC into Tech. Energy was the most net-bought sector by HFs via longs added and shorts covered. Consumer Discretionary and Real Estate were the most net sold.

bullets.title: Oil at 3-month highs ($85–$91) on US-Iran escalation; diesel near $5.85/gal record
bullets.body: US-Iran military exchanges resumed with US strikes on Iranian rocket systems and Iranian retaliatory missile strikes on US bases in Jordan and UAE. Brent briefly topped $91; US diesel hit $5.85/gallon (+55% since conflict began). Morgan Stanley raised Q4 Brent to $100/bbl. Bessent signaled 'oil prices will come down' and expects Iran to eventually negotiate. The energy shock is the single largest driver of ECB rate expectations and a key input into US inflation nowcasts currently tracking 3.5% for August.

bullets.title: September seasonality: VIX historically +22%; October VIX call spreads recommended as tail hedge
bullets.body: VIX compressed to 14.17 (near multi-year lows) heading into the seasonally weakest month for equities. Net short positioning in VIX futures is at extreme levels. 22V and Morgan Stanley both recommend buying October VIX call spreads as cheap macro tail hedges. Systematic macro strategies are at the 85th percentile of leverage, and any realized vol spike to 15% could trigger ~$80–100B of automatic equity selling.

bullets.title: August equity performance: Nasdaq +3.93%, S&P +2.62%; software (+IGV +16%) routed semis
bullets.body: The August rotation out of AI hardware/semis into software was decisive: IGV gained ~16% (best month in 2 years), while the GS High Beta Momentum basket (long semis/short software) crashed 77% from June highs. SOX finished +2% but remained 22% off its June peak. NVDA +9.8%, TSLA +18.2%, MSFT +9.2% were the Mag7 leaders; PLTR +51.5% was the standout. The equal-weight S&P only slightly lagged the cap-weighted index.

bullets.title: California utilities (PCG, EIX) collapse 20–24% as wildfire liability bill SB 492 fails
bullets.body: The California state Assembly declined to vote on SB 492, which failed to inject new capital, remove subrogation rights, or structurally de-link utility liability from wildfire fund solvency. Mizuho, Truist, and Wells Fargo all downgraded or cut price targets on PCG and EIX. Wolfe Research expects 10–15% further downside. SRE is viewed as least exposed given its Texas/LNG mix. The failure has broader implications for AI data center permitting in California.

bullets.title: Data center AI demand: global IT load CAGR 25% through 2031; regulatory backlash building pre-midterms
bullets.body: Citi forecasts IT load growing from 121 GW (2026) to 370 GW (2031). AI-driven infrastructure spending is projected at $32T by 2050. However, data center NIMBYism is spreading—New York has a state-wide moratorium, 9 states have pending moratoriums, and 20+ have restrictive legislation. Multiple analysts see this as peak regulatory headwind that fades post-November elections, with existing entitled projects (EQIX, DLR, CRWV) benefiting from supply constraints.

bullets.title: NVDA $3.5B MediaTek convertible bond investment expands NVLink Fusion ecosystem
bullets.body: NVIDIA invested $3.5B in MediaTek via convertible bonds to deepen AI partnership across cloud AI factories, local AI computing (RTX Spark), and automotive. MediaTek will adopt NVLink Fusion for custom XPU integration, which analysts view as NVIDIA positioning itself as ecosystem kingmaker—potentially creating competitive pressure on AVGO's custom ASIC franchise over the medium term.

bullets.title: Goldman Sachs shifting equities to Tactically Cautious; prefer Mag7 over AI/memory/semis near-term
bullets.body: JPM and GS both moved to cautious near-term views, recommending reducing net longs and adopting a more defensive posture into September FOMC. Within tech, both favor Mag7 over AI/memory/semis. Software is the preferred sector rotation within tech. Post-midterm election seasonality (historically SPX +5–15% at 3–12 month horizons, 78–100% hit rates) provides the medium-term bull case.

bullets.title: Tax-loss selling season begins mid-September; worst YTD performers historically underperform by 320bps
bullets.body: Wolfe Research flags the two-wave tax-loss selling pattern: mid-September through mid-October (first wave) and mid-November through mid-December (second wave). Worst-performing YTD stocks historically underperform peers by an average of 320bps during this window. NDX, MTUM, and semis already show negative 3-month momentum.

bullets.title: FHFA credit bureau action: VantageScore mandated for GSEs; FICO craters 17–18%, EFX off 10%
bullets.body: FHFA Director Pulte directed Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to approve all lenders to use VantageScore immediately, cited FICO's 1,800% price increase since 2020. FICO fell ~17%, EFX -10%, TRU -8% on the news. UBS maintains EFX Buy (PT $220) citing its 90% proprietary data and Workforce Solutions franchise; FICO and TRU at Neutral. VantageScore could open lending to 30–40M additional applicants.
